recipes.name: Spicy soft tofu stew with beef (Gogi sundubu-jjigae: 고기 순두부찌개)
ingredients: 2 cups anchovy kelp-stock stock (or beef, chicken, or vegetarian stock), recipe below.
8 ounces skirt steak (or any tender cuts of beef), chopped into small pieces
2 green onions, sliced diagonally into 1 inch long
2 tubes of sundubu (soft tofu),11 ounce each
8 large dried anchovies with the guts and heads removed
instructions: Combine the gochu-garu, sesame oil , and ground black pepper in a small bowl and mix well with a spoon.
Place the water in a stock pot. Add the anchovies, radish, and kelp. Cover and cook for 30 minutes over medium high heat. If it boils over, crack the lid.
You will get about 6 cups stock, but only need 2 cups for this recipe. Just keep the leftover stock in an airtight container and freeze it to use it in something else, or more sundubu-jjigae later.

Heat a heavy pan over medium high heat. Add the cooking oil, onion, garlic, and green onion. Stir with a wooden spoon for 3 to 4 minutes until it’s a little brown and fragrant. Stir in beef for about 2 to 3 minutes until the beef is thoroughly cooked.
Cover and cook for 6 to 7 minutes over medium heat. Open and stir in the fish sauce and salt.
Cut the tubes of soft tofu in halves and add to the soup. Add the seasoning mixture and mix, gently breaking the tofu with the wooden spoon.
Cover and cook for about 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling. Your sundubu-jjigae is then ready to serve!

instruction_sections.text: Combine the gochu-garu, sesame oil , and ground black pepper in a small bowl and mix well with a spoon.
If you use premade chicken, beef, or my vegetable stock, you can skip this process.
Place the water in a stock pot. Add the anchovies, radish, and kelp. Cover and cook for 30 minutes over medium high heat. If it boils over, crack the lid.
You will get about 6 cups stock, but only need 2 cups for this recipe. Just keep the leftover stock in an airtight container and freeze it to use it in something else, or more sundubu-jjigae later.

Cover and cook for about 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling. Your sundubu-jjigae is then ready to serve!

If you want to serve with eggs, crack one egg for each diner into the pan and let it cook for another minute without stirring or breaking the egg. Then set the pan in the middle of the table and let your family share it together with rice, kimchi, and a few more side dishes.

Divide the stew into 2 earthenware bowls and heat them up. If you want to serve with eggs, wait til the stew starts bubbling a bit before cracking them in. Let the stew cook for another 2 minutes without stirring or breaking the egg. Serve hot right away with rice, kimchi, and a few more side dishes.
